steps.title: A random variable is a function
steps.idea: Roll two dice. The outcome is a pair $\omega = (\omega_1, \omega_2)$, one of 36 equally likely cells. A random variable attaches a number to every outcome, here the sum. Outcomes with the same value pool their probability $\tfrac{1}{36}$, and the frequencies of the values settle on those pools.

layers.intuition: Each cell lights up when an experiment picks it, and a token falls into the bar of its value. The sum $7$ owns six cells, more than any other value, so its bar grows tallest.
layers.definition: A random variable is a function $X\colon \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\{\omega : X(\omega) < x\}$ is an event for every $x$. A discrete one takes values $x_1, x_2, \dots$ with probabilities $p_k = P(X = x_k)$, $\sum_k p_k = 1$.

steps.title: The distribution function
steps.idea: The distribution function collects the probability to the left of a bound: $F(x)$ adds up every $p_k$ with $x_k \le x$. For a discrete variable it is a staircase that jumps by $p_k$ at each value and stays flat in between.

layers.intuition: Type $x = 6.5$: no value lies between $6$ and $7$, so nothing changes from $x = 6$. Only crossing a value moves $F$.
layers.definition: $F(x) = P(X \le x)$ is non-decreasing, $F(-\infty) = 0$, $F(+\infty) = 1$, and $P(a < X \le b) = F(b) - F(a)$. With $\le$ it is continuous from the right: the filled dot is $F(x_k)$, the open dot the limit from the left.
layers.details: The lectures define $F(x) = P(X < x)$, which is continuous from the left. The two definitions differ only at the jumps, by $P(X = x_k)$.

steps.title: Density: probability as area
steps.idea: A continuous variable has no jumps. Its probability is spread with a density $f$, and $F(x)$ is the area under $f$ to the left of $x$. Here the exponential law, the waiting time without memory: the histogram of the draws follows its density, and the shaded area equals the height of $F$.

layers.definition: $X$ is continuous with density $f \ge 0$ if $F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\,dt$ for every $x$. Then $f(x) = F'(x)$ wherever $f$ is continuous, and $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)\,dt = 1$.
layers.details: The exponential law: $f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}$ and $F(x) = 1 - e^{-\lambda x}$ for $x \ge 0$. It has no memory: $P(X > s + t \mid X > s) = P(X > t)$.

steps.title: A single point weighs nothing
steps.idea: For a continuous law the area over a single point is zero, so $P(X = x) = 0$ for every $x$, and $<$ or $\le$ no longer matters. Probability lives on intervals: $P(a < X < b) = F(b) - F(a)$.
live: P(a < X < b) = F(b) - F(a) = \int_a^b f(t)\,dt

layers.intuition: Not one of the draws hits the bound exactly, however many there are: the empirical share of $X = x$ stays $0$.
